description: Catch-all nil for ANY Wilkins-family surname spelling, whatever the other parameters. Same problem and same shape as record-search-flynn-any-variant-no-results — read that fixture's note for the full rationale. ut_search_records_024 stocked only the exact spelling 'Wilkins', so when the skill invented 'Wilkens' or 'Wilkin' (which the Search strategy dimension rewards it for doing) the call matched nothing and came back a fixture_not_found ERROR, and Tool Arguments was scored 2 on three consecutive suite runs despite the rubric override saying to score 3. This absorbs any remaining Wilk* query and returns the honest nil instead: no estate record exists under any spelling in this scenario, so a nil is the truthful answer, not a fudge. Keep it LAST in the test's mcp_fixtures list — matching is first-match-wins in list order, so an earlier catch-all would shadow the exact 'Wilkins' fixture and erase the expected_args signal Tool Arguments is graded on. Anchored to the name stem on purpose: a search on a surname outside the Wilk* stem still misses and is still caught as a real defect. Note the limit of that guard — matches() (fixtures.py:93) checks only the keys the predicate names and ignores every other arg, so this fires on ANY query whose surname contains 'wilk', whatever the given name, place, date or collection, and it does not distinguish a plausible variant from an unrelated Wilk* surname: 'Wilkinson' matches too. That is acceptable here only because ut_search_records_024 is nil-by-design — no estate record exists under any spelling — and must be re-examined before this fixture is reused on a test that returns results. STEM GAP, deliberate: this matches the ~wilk stem only, so a vowel-substituted variant (`Welkins`) misses every fixture here and still returns fixture_not_found. That is intended — a loud miss is visible in the run log and recoverable, whereas widening the stem far enough to catch every spelling would start shadowing the specific fixtures above it. If a real run trips one, add a narrowly-anchored sibling; do not broaden this predicate.
